Thanks again for the quick intro call last week. We'd love to do a 30-minute product demo next week to walk through an inference setup aligned to KumoHealth's throughput targets. A couple of customers have bumped into calendar mismatches when invites cross local-day boundaries, so I wanted to propose times with an explicit local-time label and offer a small buffer to avoid "next-day" confusion.

Here are three slots (I've included local equivalent times):
- Option A: Wed, Jul 28 — 10:00 SGT / 11:00 JST / 12:00 AEST
- Option B: Wed, Jul 28 — 14:00 SGT / 15:00 JST / 16:00 AEST
- Option C: Thu, Jul 29 — 09:30 SGT / 10:30 JST / 11:30 AEST

Notes:
- We avoid scheduling inside the 23:30–01:30 local window (we've seen some calendar clients render those as the next calendar day).
- If none work, we can send two separate invites labeled with local dates (e.g., "SGT: Jul 28 — 10:00") so each attendee's calendar shows an explicit local string.

I attached an .ics with the three options and a short one-pager about what we'll cover. If you prefer, I can send a single confirmed invite with explicit local-time text in the subject to reduce ambiguity.

Hi Sam,

Totally understand — thanks for flagging that. A couple quick clarifications and a suggested approach:

1) The issue you saw is usually caused by an ICS generated with UTC timestamps; some calendar clients render the local date differently depending on timezone settings. The underlying UTC time was the same, but the client showed the local date as "next day" for AEST.

2) To avoid this entirely, my suggested options (pick one):
   - We move Option A earlier by 30 min to 09:30 SGT / 10:30 JST / 11:30 AEST (keeps same local day everywhere).
   - We leave Option A at 10:00 SGT but I will send two separate invites: one explicitly labeled "SGT — Jul 28 — 10:00 (UTC+8)" and another labeled "AEST — Jul 28 — 12:00 (UTC+10)". Both map to the same UTC instant but the subject makes the local date explicit for each office.

3) We also recommend a 15-minute pre/post buffer (we'll block it on our side) — we call this the "midnight buffer" rule for cross-city meetings to reduce confusion.

If you prefer the simpler path, I'll send a single confirmed invite for 09:30 SGT / 11:30 AEST (Option A moved earlier) and include the Zoom link in the calendar body plus a note: "Local times: 09:30 SGT / 10:30 JST / 11:30 AEST — all same UTC instant."

Which would you prefer?

Cheers,
Grace
